## Executive summary

Thesis in plain terms. AWS growth reaccelerated to 37 percent year over year in Q2 2026. Revenue reached 42.2 billion USD in the quarter. The annualized run rate hit 169 billion USD. Operating income reached 16.6 billion USD at a 39.4 percent margin. Ads reached 19.8 billion USD in Q2 2026, up 26 percent year over year. Retail margins grind higher on automation. That mix supports mid-teens earnings growth. So what: the 12-month path is earnings-led, not multiple-led.

Probability weights shape the target. Bear gets 20 percent weight with a 210 USD target as of the risk brief. Base gets 50 percent weight with a 300 USD target. Bull gets 25 percent weight with a 345 USD target. Tail gets 5 percent weight below 153 USD. The probability-weighted return is about plus 7 percent. Our published base target is 300 USD. That implies plus 18 percent from 254.98 USD on 2026-09-02. So what: skew is modestly positive with real drawdown risk.

Conviction is OVERWEIGHT, not maximum. The risk brief approves a 3.0 percent core weight with a 2.0 to 4.0 percent range. The hard cap is 4.0 percent. Idiosyncratic vol is 46.0 percent annualized. That drives sizing more than beta. Beta to market is 1.21. About 86 percent of variance is single-name specific. So what: keep AMZN a core slot, not a book driver.

Top catalysts are dated. Q3 earnings arrive around 2026-10-29 as an estimate. Q4 plus a Kuiper update arrive around 2027-01-28 as an estimate. The FTC bench trial starts 2027-03-29 in Seattle. AWS backlog conversion prints each quarter. Ad growth prints each quarter. So what: the calendar gives four clean re-underwriting points.

Top risks are sized. AWS share loss to Azure and GCP tops the list. Retail margin stall is second. Kuiper capex without return is third. FTC structural remedy is fourth but under 5 percent odds. A 20 percent drawdown costs 60 basis points at a 3 percent weight. So what: the position survives its own bad year.

## AWS deep dive

![AWS quarterly revenue path](charts/aws_revenue.png){#fig-ex9 width=85% fig-cap="AWS quarterly revenue — path to 42.2B in Q2 2026 (USD billions). Q2 2026 per company reports via web."}

@fig-ex9 tracks AWS revenue by quarter. The path rises from 27.5 billion USD in Q3 2024 to 42.2 billion USD in Q2 2026. Each quarter stepped higher. Q4 2025 printed about 36.5 billion USD. Q1 2026 printed about 39.0 billion USD. Q2 2026 printed 42.2 billion USD. The run rate now equals 169 billion USD annualized. That scale funds the whole AI build. So what: AWS is the engine that pays for everything else.

![AWS growth reacceleration](charts/aws_growth.png){#fig-ex10 width=85% fig-cap="AWS revenue growth — reacceleration to 37 percent (percent y/y). Q2 2026 per company reports via web."}

@fig-ex10 shows growth reacceleration. Growth rose from 12.8 percent to 37.0 percent across eight quarters. Q4 earnings showed AWS up 24 percent year over year on 2026-02-05. Q2 2026 then printed 37 percent, well above the 31 percent expected. That marked the fastest growth in 18 quarters. Backlog and AI workloads drove the jump. Enterprise migration added steady demand. So what: reacceleration is the core reason to own the stock.

![AWS margin bridge](charts/aws_margin_bridge.png){#fig-ex11 width=85% fig-cap="AWS operating margin bridge — to 39.4 percent in Q2 2026 (percent). Per company reports via web."}

@fig-ex11 bridges the margin. AWS operating income hit 16.6 billion USD in Q2 2026. That compares with 10.2 billion USD a year earlier. Margin reached 39.4 percent, up from 37.7 percent in Q1 2026. Scale and mix added about 2.5 points in our stylized walk. AI mix dragged about 1.2 points. Operating leverage then added 5.1 points into Q2. High margin on incremental AI revenue matters most. So what: growth plus margin together drive operating profit.

Bedrock and custom silicon extend the lead. Management said AI services and custom silicon each exceed 25 billion USD annualized. Both grow at triple-digit rates as of mid-2026. Trainium2 cuts training cost for enterprise clients. Inferentia cuts inference cost at scale. Bedrock hosts multiple models in one platform. Anthropic workloads add durable demand. Azure AI surges, but AWS still sets the pace on breadth. So what: silicon plus platform is a cost moat.

Backlog converts to revenue with a lag. Large enterprise deals sign first as commitments. Consumption ramps over two to four quarters. Q2 strength reflects deals signed in late 2025. That lag smooths quarterly volatility. It also backloads 2027 growth if signings hold. Watch remaining performance obligations each print. Watch consumption credits each print. So what: backlog today is revenue in early 2027.

## Retail plus automation

![Revenue mix](charts/segment_mix.png){#fig-ex14 width=70% fig-cap="Revenue mix by segment — FY2025 approx (percent of sales). Approximate from filings via web."}

@fig-ex14 splits revenue. Online plus physical retail is about 38 percent of sales. Third-party seller services are about 24 percent. AWS is about 17 percent. Ads are about 11 percent. Subscriptions are about 7 percent. Other is about 3 percent. Retail still dominates the top line. Cloud and ads dominate operating income. That split explains the whole thesis. So what: retail gives scale while cloud and ads give profit.

![Retail margin trajectory](charts/retail_margin.png){#fig-ex15 width=70% fig-cap="Retail operating margin trajectory — automation lift (percent). Stylized blend, Q2 2026."}

@fig-ex15 traces retail margin. Our stylized blend rises from 4.5 percent in Q2 2024 to 7.5 percent in Q2 2026. North America leads the gains. International follows with a lag. Robotics cut pick times in fulfillment centers. Route density cut cost per shipment. Prime fees and grocery density added mix. Each 100 basis points on retail sales is material. So what: automation turns scale into margin.

Prime resilience underpins units. Membership renewals held firm through price moves. Faster delivery windows lift order frequency. Same-day sites expanded coverage in 2025 and 2026. Regionalization shortened delivery distance. That cut cost and raised speed at once. Returns processing also improved with automation. So what: Prime is a demand anchor plus a cost lever.

Bear pushback deserves a direct answer. Retail margin could stall if wage growth reaccelerates. Fuel could spike and hit outbound cost. Discretionary units could soften in a slowdown. Our margin path assumes steady productivity gains. It does not assume price hikes. If automation stalls, the base case slips toward 270 USD. So what: track cost per unit every quarter.

## Kuiper optionality

![Kuiper rollout timeline](charts/kuiper_timeline.png){#fig-ex16 width=100% fig-cap="Project Kuiper rollout timeline — to 3,236 satellites (plan). Source: company materials via web."}

@fig-ex16 maps Kuiper milestones. Prototype flights flew in 2024. First production satellites launched in 2025. Early service is estimated for late 2025. Commercial rollout runs through 2026. Constellation build continues into 2027. The plan calls for up to 3,236 satellites. Amazon brands the network as Amazon Leo for consumers. So what: Kuiper moves from test to commercial inside our window.

![Kuiper demand curve](charts/kuiper_demand.png){#fig-ex17 width=70% fig-cap="Kuiper demand curve — stylized adoption (millions of subs). Illustrative S-curve."}

@fig-ex17 draws a stylized S-curve. Early subs grow slowly during rollout. Growth steepens as coverage fills in. Saturation comes much later. Enterprise backhaul may ramp first. Consumer dishes follow as prices fall. Government contracts could pre-fill capacity. None of this is in our base target math. So what: treat Kuiper as a free option with a visible cost.

Capex cadence is the cost of that option. The 2026 capex guide sits at 195 to 205 billion USD. Some reports cite up to 220 billion USD with memory costs. Q4 revenue printed 213.4 billion USD on 2026-02-05, up 14 percent. AWS grew 24 percent that quarter, then the fastest in 13 quarters. The market sold the guide anyway. Capex intensity now defines sentiment. Each quarter must show backlog for the spend. So what: Kuiper plus AI capex must convert or the multiple shrinks.

## Alexa plus devices plus grocery plus healthcare

Alexa+ aims at paid assistance. The pitch is an agent that shops, schedules, and controls home devices. Monetization runs through subscriptions and purchase attach. Device margins stay thin by design. The profit comes from usage, not hardware. Early reviews focus on latency and accuracy. Scale decides if it matters. Our 12-month math assigns it zero upside. So what: Alexa+ is upside only if attach proves out.

Grocery remains a long grind. Fresh formats test smaller footprints. Delivery windows keep improving in dense zones. Unit economics hinge on basket size and density. Healthcare is earlier still. Pharmacy scales best so far. Clinic buildout costs real money. Neither moves the 12-month target much. Both add terminal value if they compound. So what: keep these sections short and watch density metrics.

## Antitrust

![FTC scenario haircuts](charts/ftc_sizing.png){#fig-ex18 width=70% fig-cap="FTC scenario valuation haircut — desk sizing (percent). Desk judgment, Sep 2026."}

@fig-ex18 sizes FTC haircuts. Settlement or behavioral remedies draw a 2 to 5 percent haircut with 45 percent odds. An adverse liability finding with remedies unresolved draws 8 to 15 percent with 30 percent odds. A favorable finding draws zero with 25 percent odds. Structural remedy inside the horizon sits under 5 percent odds with a 15 to 25 percent haircut. Trial starts 2027-03-29 before Judge Chun in Seattle. A decision likely lands after 2027-09-03. Appeals run for years. So what: headline risk is real but breakup risk is remote.

A separate ad-auction suit adds noise. The FTC plus 22 states allege first-price auctions billed as second-price. Reports cite charges at the full bid about 80 percent of the time. This case is distinct from the 2023 monopolization case. Timelines overlap in headlines, not in court. Financial exposure looks manageable versus AMZN scale. Remedy would target auction mechanics. So what: separate the two cases when reading news flow.

EU DMA exposure is a fine plus a fix. Amazon is a designated gatekeeper. A Prime-practices probe was reported in November 2024. First DMA fines landed in April 2025 at 500 million EUR for Apple and 200 million EUR for Meta. A first Amazon fine likely falls in a 200 to 600 million EUR band. That is under 1 percent of equity value. The real cost is remedy drag on EU operations. Data separation and buy-box changes could dent margin by a point or two in Europe. So what: Europe is a margin irritant, not a thesis breaker.

## Capital allocation

![Capital expenditure path](charts/capex.png){#fig-ex19 width=85% fig-cap="Capital expenditure — path to about 200B in 2026 (USD billions). Guide per web, Sep 2026."}

@fig-ex19 shows capex by year. Spend was 58.3 billion USD in 2022. It eased to 52.7 billion USD in 2023. It rose to 78.0 billion USD in 2024. It jumped to about 125.0 billion USD in 2025. The 2026 guide points to about 200.0 billion USD. Memory prices pushed the top of the range. Data centers plus silicon plus Kuiper drive the total. Investors now grade every dollar. So what: capex is the single sentiment variable.

![Free cash flow bridge](charts/fcf_bridge.png){#fig-ex20 width=85% fig-cap="Free cash flow bridge — 2026 stylized (USD billions). Illustrative direction from filings."}

@fig-ex20 bridges free cash flow. Operating cash flow prints near 120 billion USD in our stylized mark. Capex consumes about 200 billion USD. Free cash flow runs negative near minus 80 billion USD. Buyback capacity adds about 15 billion USD of offset in authorization terms. Net after returns sits near minus 65 billion USD. This is a heavy investment year by choice. AWS backlog must validate it. If growth holds, the math normalizes fast. So what: 2026 FCF is depressed by design, not by distress.

Buyback math is straightforward. Authorization covers opportunistic repurchases. Pace likely stays modest during peak capex. Management prefers capacity over shrinkage now. That is the right call if returns on AI capex exceed cost of capital. Repurchases can step up once intensity eases in 2027. Rating agencies watch leverage, not buybacks. Cash generation still covers the build. So what: do not underwrite buyback-driven upside this year.

## Factor attribution

Market beta is 1.21 with a strong t-stat near 39. That marks AMZN as a high-beta growth name. HML loads at minus 0.80, a growth tilt. RMW loads at minus 0.80 in the long window. SMB loads at minus 0.17, a mega-cap tilt. Total vol runs 49.6 percent annualized on the 504-day window. Specific vol runs 46.0 percent. Common factor vol runs 18.5 percent. So what: stock-specific news moves this name more than style rotation.

Factor staleness needs disclosure. The factor mart ends 2026-06-30, about 66 days stale as of early September. Price data runs to 2026-09-02 and reads fresh. Betas describe the regime into June, not August. Direction still holds for sizing. Magnitude needs a refresh after next earnings. The 14 percent factor variance share passes our 40 percent veto standalone. A full Mag-7 sleeve would breach it at about 55 percent. So what: cap the mega-cap sleeve at 15 percent of book.

## Bull versus bear debate

Bull case stacks three drivers. AWS grows in the mid-teens or better with margin near 39 percent. Ads compounds above 20 percent with high incremental margin. Retail automation adds 100 basis points or more. Together they push operating income sharply higher. Consensus targets up to 353 USD reflect that math. Backlog conversion in early 2027 seals it. Invalidation is clean if AWS drops under 20 percent. So what: bulls need execution, not miracles.

Bear case stacks four kills. Azure and GCP take AI share with tighter enterprise bundles. Retail margin stalls on wages and fuel. Kuiper burns capex without revenue through 2027. The FTC forces harsh remedies after the March 2027 trial. Any two together push AMZN toward 210 USD. All four together open the tail under 153 USD. Bears are wrong if AWS holds 30 percent growth. Bears are wrong if ads holds 25 percent. So what: bears need two breaks to win.

We settle the debate in favor of the base. AWS at 37 percent in Q2 2026 favors bulls near-term. Capex at 200 billion USD favors bears on FCF. Ads at 26 percent favors bulls on mix. FTC timing past the horizon favors base patience. Net leans bullish on earnings with a sizing leash. That is why the call is OVERWEIGHT at 3 percent. It is not a full-bore BUY at 4 percent. So what: own the compounding, respect the spend.

## Final recommendation

We rate AMZN OVERWEIGHT to 300 USD by 2027-09-03. That is plus 18 percent from 254.98 USD on 2026-09-02. Own 3 percent with a 2 to 4 percent range and a 4 percent hard cap. Cap the combined Mag-7 sleeve at 15 percent of book. Re-run risk after each earnings print. Cut on trough failure, not on noise. So what: this is research, not financial advice, sized to survive its own risks.

What changes our mind. AWS growth under 20 percent for two quarters flips us to NEUTRAL. Retail margin rolling over for two quarters flips us to NEUTRAL. A structural FTC order inside the horizon flips us to UNDERWEIGHT. Sustained 30 percent AWS growth with margin beats flips us to BUY toward 345 USD. Until then, hold the base. So what: four triggers decide the next twelve months.

## Demand deep dive

Enterprise consumption drives AWS first. Lift-and-shift migration still fills the base. New AI workloads add the growth on top. Bedrock lets firms test many models fast. That shortens sales cycles from months to weeks. Credits convert to commits when pilots hit production. Q2 2026 showed that flip at scale. Consumption growth beat the 31 percent expected pace. It printed 37 percent year over year. So what: pilots turned into production spend.

Backlog quality matters more than backlog size. Multi-year commits with annual ramps are the best kind. Take-or-pay terms with usage floors come next. Loose credits with no floor rank last. Our read of Q2 is that mix improved. Large deals from late 2025 started consuming in early 2026. That lag explains the step up from 24 percent in Q4 to 37 percent in Q2. Watch RPO growth versus revenue growth each quarter. If RPO leads, revenue follows. So what: backlog composition predicts the next two quarters.

Ad budget share gains rest on measurement. Merchants shift spend where sales attribution is cleanest. Amazon links an ad click to a purchase in one system. That closed loop wins budgets from open-web display. Video supply on Prime adds brand dollars too. Sponsored listings still drive the core. Offsite placements extend reach without losing attribution. The 26 percent growth in Q2 2026 reflects that edge. Meta and Google grew slower on our marks. So what: measurement is the share-gain engine.

Retail units held up through automation. Same-day fulfillment lifted conversion in covered zips. Regional inventory cut split shipments. That lowered cost per box while raising speed. Robotics in pick and pack cut labor hours per unit. Route optimization raised stops per hour. Each lever adds a few dozen basis points. Stacked over eight quarters, they add points. Our stylized retail margin rose from 4.5 to 7.5 percent. That path needs steady execution, not price hikes. So what: productivity funds margin without taxing demand.

Kuiper demand starts with backhaul and ends with homes. Telecom carriers buy capacity where fiber does not reach. Governments buy resilience for remote sites. Enterprises buy backup links for critical facilities. Consumers come last as terminal prices fall. Early capacity may sell below cost to seed the base. That is normal for networks. Unit cost falls as launch cadence rises. Our S-curve assumes slow start then steep ramp. We assign it no 12-month earnings credit. So what: demand exists but timing is uncertain.

Prime demand stays the retail anchor. Renewal rates held firm as of mid-2026 reports. Delivery speed gains lift order frequency. Grocery attach raises basket size. Pharmacy attach raises visit frequency. Each adds a small lift to units. Together they stabilize growth through cycles. A job-market shock would still dent discretionary units. Essentials and subscriptions would cushion the fall. That mix is why retail deserves a mid-single growth credit. So what: Prime smooths the cycle.

What would break the demand read. Enterprise IT freezes would stall consumption fast. Ad agency holds would cut brand budgets first. A parcel cost shock would squeeze retail margin. Kuiper terminal delays would push revenue right. None of these show in Q2 2026 prints. Each needs a quarterly check. The catalyst calendar gives those checkpoints. So what: demand is strong but verified quarterly.

## Competition: Azure and GCP up close

Azure sells the bundle. Microsoft pairs OpenAI access with Office distribution. That combo wins centralized IT shops. Seat-based pricing makes adoption easy to approve. Co-pilot attach pulls Azure consumption with it. Azure AI growth has run hot into 2026. That pressures AWS on new AI logos. AWS answers with broader model choice and silicon cost. The race is speed versus distribution. So what: AWS must win on cost per token.

GCP sells the data edge. BigQuery plus Vertex attract analytics-led firms. Google models win on specific multimodal tasks. Price cuts keep pressure on inference rates. GCP share gains show in AI-native startups. AWS counters with Bedrock breadth and Trainium price. Enterprise scorecards now track cost per million tokens. They also track latency at peak load. Silicon decides both over time. So what: Trainium is a competitive weapon, not a lab project.

Retail competition splits by lane. Walmart wins on grocery value and store density. Costco wins on treasure hunt and membership loyalty. Shein and Temu pressure low-ticket discretionary. Amazon wins on selection plus speed plus Prime. Ad load is the swing factor to watch. Too many sponsored slots could hurt conversion. Too few leaves margin on the table. Our base assumes a balanced load. So what: retail moat is logistics, not price alone.

Cloud share math frames the debate. AWS holds the largest revenue base as of Q2 2026. Azure grows fast off a smaller AI-heavy mix. GCP grows fast off the smallest base. Share headlines thus mislead in any single quarter. Absolute dollar adds matter more for profit. AWS added the most dollars in Q2 on our read. That is what funds capex. Bears cite share loss in AI workloads. Bulls cite dollar adds across all workloads. So what: count dollars, not headlines.

## Operating model and margin bridge

Company margin blends three very different units. Retail runs on single-digit margins with huge sales. Third-party services run richer on take rates. AWS runs near 39 percent with scale. Ads runs the richest on incremental dollars. Mix shift toward AWS and ads lifts the total every year. That is why revenue mix matters more than revenue growth alone. One point of mix beats one point of growth. So what: follow the mix, not just the top line.

Our stylized company bridge runs clean. Start near 10 percent operating margin in early 2025. Add 1.5 points from AWS mix and scale. Add 1.2 points from ads mix. Add 0.8 points from retail automation. Subtract 0.5 points from Kuiper and content spend. Land near 13 percent by late 2026. Each piece is small alone. Together they compound. If any piece stalls, growth must work harder. So what: margin has four small engines, not one big bet.

Sensitivity keeps us honest. If AWS growth runs 5 points light, operating income misses by high single digits. If ads growth runs 5 points light, the miss is mid single digits. If retail margin stalls flat, the miss is low single digits. Stack all three and the base target slips to about 270 USD. That is still above the 210 USD bear. It sits well below the 345 USD bull. Position size handles that band. So what: the base survives one miss, not three.

## Balance sheet and cash discipline

Cash generation stays robust through the build. Operating cash flow covers most capex even in 2026. Debt capacity remains ample for a mega cap. Lease obligations fund fulfillment and data centers. Working capital benefits from marketplace float. Negative FCF in 2026 reflects choice, not stress. That distinction matters for credit. Rating headroom stays intact. So what: the balance sheet funds the option.

Discipline shows in allocation order. Data center capacity comes first. Custom silicon comes second. Fulfillment automation comes third. Kuiper launches come fourth. Buybacks come last in a peak year. That order maximizes return on each dollar. It also matches payback speed. AI capacity pays back fastest if backlog holds. Kuiper pays back slowest by design. Investors should judge each bucket alone. So what: grade capex by bucket, not as one lump.

## Governance and execution risk

Leadership continuity anchors execution. AWS leadership depth matters most for delivery. Retail operations depth matters for margin. Turnover in either would slow the plan. Succession bench reads solid from outside. Key-person risk centers on continuity of the AI build. Hiring pace in silicon and Bedrock teams signals health. Attrition spikes would warn early. No such signal shows as of September 2026. So what: execution risk is normal, not elevated.

Cost control needs the same gaze. Headcount growth should trail revenue growth. Stock comp should stay near plan as a share of sales. Marketing spend should track ad revenue growth. Overhead should scale slower than gross profit. Q2 2026 prints fit that pattern. Any sharp break would flag bloat. Quarterly filings give the check. So what: growth with discipline sustains the multiple.

## Managing the position through the year

Revisit the thesis at each earnings print. Update AWS growth first. Update ads second. Update retail margin third. If two of three beat, hold the 3 percent weight. If two of three miss, trim to 2 percent. Earnings dates move, so confirm each date two weeks out. Use the levels in the trading plan between prints. Do not add on FTC headlines alone. Add only on backlog strength with margin intact. Take profit toward 345 USD if the move comes fast. That keeps the book balanced into 2027. Discipline here matters more than any single forecast. So what: process protects the gain.
